text:
alice: Quick sync — proposal to consolidate telemetry fields `route_id` + `route_key` into a single canonical `route_ref` ahead of the new routing policy. Goal: simplify downstream dashboards, reduce join complexity, and make quota-routing lookups deterministic. Thoughts?
ben: +1 on simplicity. main concern is console query compatibility and p99 regressions on the dashboard card queries that currently filter on `route_key`.
carol: Can we do a dual-write (old fields kept, new `route_ref` populated) and then backfill? That reduces breakage for consumers.
dave: I sketched a backfill job — plan is shadow-write for 48h then run a chunked backfill. Example SQL for backfill we used previously:```sql
-- backfill route_ref from existing fields
UPDATE analytics.events
SET route_ref = COALESCE(route_key, route_id::text)
WHERE route_ref IS NULL
AND created_at < now() - interval '5m';
```
eva: Important: dashboards that group by route will need index support. If we just add the new column without an index, queries will p99 spike during the reindex. We should schedule a concurrent index on `route_ref` before switching console defaults.
ben: Agreed. Also need to update any saved queries/alerts in the console. We should run a migration that rewrites saved queries to prefer `route_ref` when available but keep a fallback to `route_key`.
carol: For rollout UX, propose a console toggle under Debug -> "Prefer route_ref" that devs can flip. Default stays false until we've validated the backfill and index. Once dual-write + backfill + index done, flip for a canary org, monitor.
adave: (typo) dave: I'll own the backfill orchestration and can run it from the migration runner. ETA to craft job: tomorrow morning.
infra-bot: Preflight checks: schema-change plan uploaded -> https://redwood-internal/changes/1823; CI checks passed for migration script.
job-bot: Migration job scheduled in dev cluster: migration-1823-backfill -> starts 2025-06-06T02:00Z.
ben: A few edgecases: 1) some old events have both fields null (rare) — we should decide default semantics (set `route_ref` to `unknown` or leave null). 2) downstream join keys (quota service) may still read `route_id` typed as bigint, we need a compatibility cast layer.
carol: For (1) let's set `route_ref = 'unknown'` on backfill and raise a metric (route_ref:unknown) so owners can inspect. For (2) add a read-adapter in the quota service that prefers `route_ref` and falls back to `route_id` cast. We'll coordinate with quota owners.
dave: Backfill plan outline: 1) add column `route_ref` (nullable) 2) start dual-write in API layer for 48h -> shadow writes to route_ref 3) create concurrent index on `route_ref` 4) run chunked backfill with metric emission 5) flip console canary toggle for 5% orgs 6) monitor query latency and errors 7) swap default and clean old fields after 30d
eva: Reindex timing: creating concurrent index on a large table still has IO impact. Recommend running index creation during off-peak and watch replica catch-up. Also consider building index on a partitioned slice if possible.
alice: UX note: we should add a migration notice in the Console release notes and a temporary deprecation banner for saved query editors: "route_key will be consolidated into route_ref in ~30 days; please prefer route_ref".
ben: I'll scan the alerting rules and list ones that reference `route_key`. We can auto-rewrite when safe but need manual approval.
carol: Metrics to watch: console p99 query latency (by card), failed query rate, count of `route_ref = 'unknown'`, number of saved queries touched, quota-service 5xxs.
dave: I will add a healthcheck endpoint in the backfill job that posts progress to #eng-platform-migrations. Job will also emit to prometheus: `migration.route_ref_backfill_progress` and `migration.route_ref_errors`.
infra-bot: Heads-up: rolling change requires migration-runner permission group. Alice, confirm you want devops to create the job RBAC.
alice: Yes please, grant migration-runner to @dave and @job-bot.
ben: One more: analytics ingestion pipeline (stream processors) that normalize route fields — update them to populate `route_ref` on ingest so eventually older partitions don't require backfill for new traffic.
carol: Timeline proposal: dual-write + index + small canary in 72 hours, full backfill over the following 7 days, default flip at ~day 10 if metrics are clean. Post-flip, keep old fields around for 30 days then drop.
dave: OK I'll post a detailed runbook tomorrow with exact SQL, chunk sizes, and throttling knobs.
eva: I can schedule the concurrent index window and coordinate with SRE for IO guardrails.
alice: thanks everyone — seems we have owners. If no blockers I'll open the migration PR and the runbook.
ben: minor nit — update the SDK docs (python/js) to include `route_ref` examples for filter helpers.
carol: I'll take the console toggle implementation and migrations of saved queries.
job-bot: NOTE: migration-1823-backfill queued -> check https://ci.redwood/migrations/1823 for logs.
